projects.title: Operations Dashboard
projects.summary: One daily view of localization operations data that previously lived in separate tools.
projects.problem: Request, translation-volume and cost-efficiency data sat in different systems, so answering a simple operational question meant stitching sources together by hand.
projects.contribution: Built the dashboard end to end: the SQL data layer, the metric logic, the app, and a natural-language “Ask the data” feature that uses the same metric definitions as the cards.
implementation: Next.js, React and TypeScript app running on Snowflake App Runtime (SPCS)
SQL data layer joining Phrase TMS and Wrike data with fiscal-quarter logic
Dynamic Tables to precompute heavy job-level calculations
Semantic View + Cortex Agent so dashboard cards and natural-language answers share one metric definition
Per-question usage logging, role-based access, daily usage email and metric documentation
Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui and Recharts UI; deployed with Snowflake CLI
notes: Precomputing with Dynamic Tables was described as reducing page-load timeouts; no improvement figure is claimed here.

ai.note: Semantic View + Cortex Agent natural-language questions.

data.note: SQL data layer, fiscal-quarter logic, precomputation with Dynamic Tables.

app.note: Next.js · React · TypeScript app with Tailwind, shadcn/ui and Recharts.

ops.note: App Runtime deployment, role-based access, usage logging and daily usage report.

projects.title: Phrase TMS Ingestion Pipeline
projects.summary: Collects job and workflow history from an external TMS and turns “translated work” into an agreed, reproducible count.
projects.problem: Translation volume was reported from several places with different rules, so the same quarter could produce different numbers.
projects.contribution: Designed and built the ingestion, the historical backfill and the single SQL definition of what counts, then documented it for the team.
implementation: Phrase TMS API → Snowflake with Snowpark Python stored procedures
External Access Integration and managed secrets for the outbound API calls
Job, workflow-step and status-change history, run daily by a Snowflake Task DAG
Backfill of step-level history covering two fiscal years
The team’s counting rules encoded in one SQL view, with approval-backed inclusion and exclusion lists
Dated snapshot tables that freeze published quarterly figures
Dependency checks before retiring legacy views
Cross-checks against independent trackers and Wrike history
notes: Wrike data reached this pipeline through a Fivetran-synced cache. I used and mapped the synced data; building or operating the Fivetran connector was not part of my role.
The backfill was reported as completing without API call failures. That is a self-reported result, not an independently verified one.

data.note: API ingestion, two-year backfill, counting rules as a SQL view, dated snapshots, reconciliation.

app.note: External API integration through External Access Integration.

ops.note: Daily Task DAG, approval-backed exceptions, dependency checks, documentation.

projects.summary: Connects transcription, translation, rule-based subtitle formatting, human review and video burn-in.
projects.problem: Subtitling mixed AI steps, strict formatting rules and human judgement, and each was handled separately.
projects.contribution: Built the pipeline and the review app, separated model decisions from deterministic formatting, and packaged a self-service edition for other teams.

projects.title: Content Search Assistant
projects.summary: A multilingual Slack assistant for finding localized content.
projects.problem: Colleagues in different languages struggled to find the right piece of content quickly.
projects.contribution: Built and operated it end to end — search data, agent, Slack app and deployment — and improved it from query logs.
implementation: Cortex Agent orchestration over eight tools (three Cortex Search services, five SQL UDFs)
Keyword search (ILIKE) first; semantic search (snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5) when keyword search finds nothing
Language-inference priority, tool-routing rules and response-format constraints
Search text combining title, tags, industry and product; metadata recovered from URL paths
Diagnosed a metric discontinuity caused by an upstream data change
Python Slack Bolt app over Socket Mode: Home tab, Block Kit, DM commands, mentions, modal filters
Eight languages, CJK spacing normalisation and Slack mrkdwn handling
Docker (linux/amd64) images, versioning and rolling deployment on SPCS; managed with Snowflake CLI and the agent-studio CLI
Usage logging → zero-result query analysis → fixes → redeploy
notes: Retrieval is multi-stage: keyword first, then semantic as a fallback. Results are not fused or reranked, so this is not hybrid retrieval.
Query-log work reduced the zero-result rate — the share of searches that return nothing. That is not a measure of search accuracy or answer correctness.

concepts.name: Grain
concepts.definition: What one row — or one counted unit — represents.
concepts.inPractice: Translation work can be counted per job, per workflow step or per completed piece of work; choosing the unit is what makes a count reproducible.
concepts.question: What exactly is being counted once?

concepts.name: Semantic Layer
concepts.definition: A shared definition of metrics, dimensions and relationships that every consumer uses.
concepts.inPractice: The dashboard, the agent and the analytics skills read the same definitions, so the same question gets the same number.
concepts.question: Is the same question calculated the same way everywhere?

concepts.name: Snapshot
concepts.definition: A record that freezes a state or result at a point in time.
concepts.inPractice: Published quarterly figures are frozen so they can be reproduced later, even as live data keeps changing.
concepts.question: Why does the published number differ from the live one?

concepts.name: Reconciliation
concepts.definition: Comparing figures from separate sources and explaining the differences.
concepts.inPractice: Ingested counts were cross-checked against independent trackers and against the dashboard and skills.
concepts.question: Is a difference a missing record or a different definition?

concepts.name: Backfill
concepts.definition: Filling in historical data after the fact.
concepts.inPractice: Step-level history for two fiscal years was loaded after the daily pipeline was in place.
concepts.question: How do you know the backfilled period is complete?

concepts.name: DAG (task dependencies)
concepts.definition: A graph of tasks and their dependencies with no cycles.
concepts.inPractice: Daily ingestion runs as a Snowflake Task DAG so each step waits for the one it depends on.
concepts.question: What happens downstream when an upstream task fails?

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.definition: Running the same operation again leaves the system in the same state.
concepts.inPractice: Relevant wherever jobs are re-run or retried — ingestion re-runs and translation-job retries.
concepts.question: Is a retry safe if the first response was lost?

concepts.name: Retry, timeout and polling
concepts.definition: Trying again after failure, bounding how long to wait, and checking job status on an interval.
concepts.inPractice: Translation jobs are submitted, polled, retried and validated against an asynchronous API.
concepts.question: Which errors should never be retried?

concepts.name: Fallback
concepts.definition: Switching to an alternative path when the primary one fails or returns nothing.
concepts.inPractice: Subtitle translation falls back between models; content search falls back from keyword to semantic search.
concepts.question: What triggers the switch, and how do results differ?

concepts.name: Multi-stage vs. hybrid retrieval
concepts.definition: Multi-stage retrieval runs search steps in sequence under conditions; hybrid retrieval combines results from different methods.
concepts.inPractice: The content search assistant is multi-stage: keyword first, semantic only when keyword finds nothing. It does not fuse or rerank results.
concepts.question: Is there an actual step that combines results?

concepts.name: Embeddings
concepts.definition: Numerical representations that let text be compared by meaning.
concepts.inPractice: Semantic search over content uses an embedding model through Cortex Search.
concepts.question: Does “similar” mean “correct”?

concepts.name: Tool routing
concepts.definition: Choosing which tool to call, with which arguments, for a request.
concepts.inPractice: The search agent routes between search services and SQL functions under explicit routing rules.
concepts.question: Can a wrong answer be told apart from a wrong tool choice?

concepts.name: Evaluation vs. testing
concepts.definition: Tests check code behaviour against expected outputs; evaluations judge model or agent behaviour against criteria.
concepts.inPractice: Regression tests guard the subtitle pipeline and the analytics app; evaluation scenarios were designed for the QA exception planner but not yet run.
concepts.question: Is this checking code, or judging behaviour?

concepts.name: Regression test
concepts.definition: A check that existing behaviour still works after a change.
concepts.inPractice: Subtitle formatting rules are protected by regression tests.
concepts.question: Which change is this test meant to catch?

concepts.name: Human-in-the-loop
concepts.definition: Designing where a person reviews or decides within an automated flow.
concepts.inPractice: Subtitle drafts go through browser review before burn-in; the QA exception planner defines hand-off to a person as a design concern.
concepts.question: When, to whom and with what is work handed over?

concepts.name: Deterministic processing
concepts.definition: Processing that gives the same output for the same input and rules.
concepts.inPractice: Translation is left to the model; line length, timing and line breaks are handled by deterministic rules.
concepts.question: Why separate model judgement from rule processing?

concepts.name: Caching and precomputation
concepts.definition: Reusing results, or computing them ahead of time.
concepts.inPractice: A per-user query cache in Content Journey; Dynamic Tables precompute heavy calculations for the dashboard.
concepts.question: When does a cached result expire, and whose access does it respect?

concepts.name: Authentication, authorization and execution rights
concepts.definition: Who someone is; what they may do; and whose privileges a procedure runs with.
concepts.inPractice: OAuth and secrets for service auth, RBAC for apps, and owner’s or caller’s rights chosen per data domain.
concepts.question: Does a successful login mean data access is allowed?

concepts.name: Observability
concepts.definition: Understanding a system’s behaviour from its logs and state.
concepts.inPractice: Usage logs, freshness indicators and scheduled usage reports across the apps and skills.
concepts.question: Can a failure be told apart from no one using it?

concepts.name: Zero-result rate
concepts.definition: The share of searches that return no results.
concepts.inPractice: Used to find and fix gaps in the content search assistant. It measures coverage of queries, not accuracy or relevance.
concepts.question: Are the denominator, period and comparison the same?

concepts.name: CI and release management
concepts.definition: Automated checks on changes, and managing versioned releases.
concepts.inPractice: Feature branches with automated PR checks, semantic versioning and a changelog for Content Journey.
concepts.question: Is passing tests the same as a successful release?
